Article Title: Oil prices dip marginally as US weighs easing sanctions on ‘shadow fleet’ tankers
Article Text:
Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel

Oil prices fell slightly on Friday as investors weighed rising tensions in the Middle East against the possibility of the US easing restrictions on ships carrying oil from sanctioned countries. Brent crude stood at $105.40, a decline of 0.52% while WTI crude was trading at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%.The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. WTI settled more than 3% higher on Thursday, supported by a significant reduction in US crude inventories. Brent, however, finished the session with little change.Efforts to increase supplies have also failed to fully ease market concerns. On Thursday, the International Energy Agency agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel, alongside any oil left over from the record emergency reserve release announced in March. The move was intended to increase availability and bring down soaring prices.Another major factor under consideration is a possible change in US sanctions policy. The Trump administration is discussing whether to lift restrictions on certain vessels in the so-called “shadow fleet”, which has carried oil and petroleum products from Russia, Iran and Venezuela, a US official said on Wednesday, as cited by Reuters.The proposed step is aimed at easing record-high global freight rates.The deliberations follow US President Donald Trump’s temporary lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel fuel. The decision prompted criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some Republicans in the US Senate.Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market. The intensifying conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis, along with fresh attacks on ships in the region, has provided support to oil prices.Attacks around the waterway have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and stricter sanctions imposed last month.The violence also spread to Yemen’s southern city of Aden on Thursday, when the Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex, killing two guards. Separately, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure as the conflict continued to escalate.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $105.40 per barrel on Friday, a decline of 0.52%. WTI crude was at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%. The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market.

Article Title: India raises petrol export duty fivefold to Rs 2.5/litre, cuts diesel levy to Rs 8.5
Article Text:
Govt raises petrol export duty, cuts diesel levy

NEW DELHI: The government has raised the export duty on petrol fivefold to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5, while cutting the levy on diesel to Rs 8.5 per litre from Rs 16. The revised rates came into effect on October 16.The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre, according to a finance ministry notification issued on Friday.The revised rates cover the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), with no road and infrastructure cess (RIC) applicable on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF. The changes follow the previous revision, which took effect on October 1.Export duties on the three petroleum products are reviewed every fortnight, with rates determined by average international prices of crude oil and the respective fuels during the period since the last review. The latest revision changes the levies on petrol and diesel in opposite directions, while leaving the ATF duty unchanged.The revised export duties will not affect the existing excise duty rates on petrol and diesel sold for domestic consumption.India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026 as crude oil prices surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran.The tax was intended to discourage exports and protect domestic supplies of petroleum products amid the conflict in the Middle East. It was also aimed at preventing exporters from benefiting unduly from differences between domestic and international prices as global crude oil prices rose.The government imposed export duties on diesel and ATF on March 27, 2026, and introduced the levy on petrol exports from May 16. Rates have since been reviewed every fortnight.
Article Summary: The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre. India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026.

Article Title: India-China trade jumps 29% to $91.76 billion, overtakes US in first half of FY27
Article Text:
Representative image (India-China trade rebounds as New Delhi looks to rebuild bilateral ties)

India-US trade rises, but surplus narrows

India looks to rebuild trade ties with China

Exports rise across markets in first half of FY27

India’s bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion in April-September 2026-27, making Beijing India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the financial year, according to commerce ministry data.Two-way trade between India and China stood at $71.24 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.China moved ahead of the US, with India’s trade with Washington rising 16.5 per cent to $83.14 billion during the first six months of the current fiscal year, compared with $71.39 billion a year earlier.India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period. Imports from China grew 27.82 per cent to $80.34 billion, against $62.86 billion previously.The faster growth in imports widened India’s trade deficit with China to $68.93 billion in the first half of FY27, from $54.06 billion in the corresponding period last year, the data showed.India’s bilateral trade with the US increased to $83.14 billion in April-September 2026-27 from $71.39 billion in the year-ago period.Exports to the US rose 11.11 per cent to $50.81 billion from $45.73 billion, while imports increased 25.98 per cent to $32.32 billion from $25.66 billion, according to the commerce ministry data.As imports grew faster than exports, India’s trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.49 billion from $20.07 billion in the first half of 2025-26.Despite tariff-related disruptions, the US remained India’s largest merchandise export destination during the period. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction and that both sides were working to conclude it at the earliest.“The negotiations are in the right direction. Probably, we are in a very good zone. We anticipate closing the deal and signing it at the earliest possible time,” Agrawal said.He said the agreement would depend on the finalisation of the broader US tariff framework, with a parallel process underway under Section 301. India is seeking preferential access to the American market to help its exporters compete with those from other countries, he added.The increase in trade with China comes as New Delhi signals efforts to improve bilateral relations. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday that India was working to rebuild its relationship with China, but the last word on the process had not yet been scripted.Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal also said the two countries were in contact on trade-related issues.“There are discussions going on on both sides on trade issues also...constant discussions will help improve the trade ties between the two countries,” he told reporters, according to news agency PTI.The commerce ministry data also showed substantial changes in India’s trade with other countries during April-September 2026-27.Exports to Singapore rose 103 per cent, while shipments to Tanzania increased 122.5 per cent. However, exports to the UAE, the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia declined.On the imports side, inbound shipments from Oman rose 210.9 per cent, while imports from Brazil increased sharply, with the data citing a rise of 143.13 per cent. Imports from the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Switzerland declined.Separately, India’s merchandise exports rose 23.04 per cent year-on-year to $44.4 billion in September, while imports increased 8 per cent to $74.61 billion, according to government data.The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion in September from $33 billion a year earlier, although it widened from $26.86 billion in August.Cumulatively, merchandise exports rose 18.51 per cent to $259.89 billion during April-September 2026-27, while imports increased 16.31 per cent to $437.53 billion. The trade deficit for the first half of the fiscal year widened to $177.64 billion from $156.88 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.Agrawal said exports were maintaining their growth trend and expressed hope that merchandise exports could exceed $500 billion if the momentum continued. India’s merchandise exports stood at $442 billion in 2025-26.
Article Summary: Bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion. India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period.

Article Title: Elon Musk's monopoly charge, Reliance's response: What's the Starlink-Jio row all about?
Article Text:
Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink

Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry

Government asks Starlink to comply with law

NEW DELHI: Reliance Industries has welcomed Elon Musk ’s Starlink to India, saying it has never feared competition and that its own satellite services are also in the queue.The statement comes as a response to Musk’s repeated allegations that vested interests were obstructing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.In a statement released on Friday, the company said India’s investment and innovation landscape was open to both domestic and foreign players, with the same regulatory process applying to all applicants.The statement, posted on social media platform X, stated, “In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio 's own satellite services await clearances.”The telecom firm further added, “At Reliance, we have never feared competition.We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”Reliance’s statement came after SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk accused the Indian conglomerate of benefiting from the existing market structure and alleged that arguments against Starlink’s entry were contradictory.In a post on X, Musk had said, "The ridiculous arguments by Ambani’s army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole."Musk argued that greater competition would give Indian consumers more choices, even if it reduced the profits of existing players. However, he said, this would not necessarily threaten their businesses."The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," he wrote.Musk had previously alleged monopolistic practices in India’s telecommunications market and questioned the regulatory barriers facing Starlink’s commercial launch in the country.In another post, he directly addressed the government, writing, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?"The government has denied Musk’s allegation that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said that there is no question of allowing a monopoly in satellite communications. He also said three entities are in line for final approval for commercial licences.Scindia said that India was close to taking a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services. All licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before beginning commercial operations.Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch its services in India because it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to establish domestic infrastructure, a senior government official said earlier this week.The government has no objection to the company rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations, sources said.A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the “first hop”, connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to establish base stations is intended to help authorities ensure compliance with the law.Reliance Jio, Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Musk’s Starlink are the three entities planning to launch satellite communication services in India.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal has also said that Airtel’s satellite venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, could receive regulatory approval before Starlink because it applied earlier and is further along in the process.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink. Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.

Article Title: Rs 1 crore-plus salaries: Amid layoffs, which Indian IT sector jobs are getting huge salary premiums?
Article Text:
Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior.

Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior. Which roles are in demand? What are the average salary levels for special capability sets and which roles are under pressure?

What are the salary levels for those getting hired at premiums?

AI’s Role Disruption Map

Entry level salaries

The report lists annual salaries of Rs 1.08 crore for AI Architects, Rs 1.02 crore for Industrial Data Architects and Rs 95.8 lakh for OT Security Architects. These figures reflect the value that is being placed on designing, securing and governing complex technology systems, beyond coding alone.

Entry-level salaries for Tier 2 AI-Adjacent

Entry level salaries for Tier 3 AI-Support

So, what can IT sector professionals do?

At the entry level, he says professionals with strong foundations in software engineering, data and AI application can distinguish themselves through practical implementation skills.

At the mid-career level, expertise in areas such as AI engineering, machine learning operations and enterprise AI integration becomes particularly valuable as organisations look to move beyond experimentation towards deployment at scale.

At the senior level, compensation increasingly reflects the ability to architect enterprise AI systems, lead transformation programmes and ensure that technology investments deliver measurable business outcomes, he adds.

Early and Mid Career Salary Trends Across Roles

Biggest takeaway

For early-career professionals, this means building strong technical fundamentals while gaining hands-on experience in AI, data and cloud technologies.

For mid-career professionals, the priority is to move beyond execution and develop the ability to integrate technologies, improve workflows and translate domain expertise into scalable solutions.

For senior professionals, the focus must extend to strategic decision-making, enterprise-wide AI adoption, governance and the ability to connect technology investments with business performance, he says.

AI capability maturity framework: From skills to salary premiums

Till a few years ago, software engineers in India were commanding high salary premiums and the IT sector was a reliable source of employment. While still employing lakhs, the artificial intelligence-led disruptions have meant that there is growing uncertainty on the relevance of traditional IT sector roles.As Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital says, “Every few years, the labour market crosses a threshold that is easy to miss in the moment and impossible to reverse in hindsight. India's digital workforce crossed one this year.”“This landscape brings immense opportunity, but it also collapses old certainties about how talent is valued. Job titles and role definitions are becoming less reliable indicators of capability or compensation,” she says.The fundamental point to understand is that India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill-differentiated compensation; with specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable.According to a TeamLease Digital report on Digital Skills and Salary Primer FY2026-27, there is a widening pay gap in India’s technology sector, with premiums increasingly going to professionals who can build, integrate, secure and manage AI systems. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.The premium concentrates in four families, AI, Data, Cloud and Cybersecurity, and peaks where capability depth meets governance and scale.And, this divide is visible across AI skill tiers. For example, the report puts entry-level median pay for AI-core roles at Rs 13.2 lakh, compared with Rs 9-10.2 lakh for AI-adjacent roles and Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh for AI-support roles. The projected salary growth is 16-21% for AI-core, against 13-18% for AI-adjacent and 7-8% for AI-support.Not only that, the premiums also extend to architecture, data and cybersecurity. The report says that skills such as GenAI engineers, AI architects, ML platform and cloud security are the highest in demand.“The 108.6 LPA figure is the median for AI Architects with 15+ years in our analysis of 37,000 roles. It reflects a senior role, not a market-wide norm. The differentiator is the ability to own architecture, scale production systems, manage risk, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes,” explains Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital.Also, geographies no longer define premiums as much. For example, according to the report, a GenAI engineer in Indore earns around Rs 16.5 lakh per annum, and out-earns cybersecurity talent in Bengaluru that gets Rs 14.4 lakh.Milind Shah, Managing Director, Randstad Digital - India tells TOI that the compensation for niche AI roles can vary considerably depending on the depth of expertise, role complexity and business impact. On an average, talent with niche tech skills may command anywhere between a 10-25% premium.Why are these roles commanding a premium? It’s a mix of skill shortage and the roles themselves generating more business value that routine IT jobs no longer are.According to Neeti Sharma, only about 16% of India’s IT professionals hold AI skills, so the supply is thin. She explains that companies are not able to find people who can take AI from pilot to production and stand accountable for it.“But this is not wage inflation. The market is pricing roles whose output is the AI system itself, which makes them the hardest to substitute. Routine support keeps operations running, and that is the layer AI is compressing first. Employers are paying for scarcity, and for people who can own the outcome,” she tells TOI.Reskilling is central to the shift. The TeamLease report points to pathways such as moving testers into intelligent operations, analysts into decision intelligence, and mid-career professionals into platform, product, governance and architecture roles.Its broader message is that combining core technical expertise with AI skills, domain knowledge and business judgement will increasingly determine salary growth.Milind Shah shares strategies for every level:So, what does this mean for tech professionals? The biggest takeaway is that professionals need to shift from being defined by the roles they perform to the capabilities they bring to the business.“As AI becomes embedded across technology functions, the value of talent will increasingly depend on the ability to adapt, solve complex problems and apply emerging technologies to real-world business challenges,” Milind Shah says.For people who are in traditional IT sector roles, it’s important to understand that while the jobs are not disappearing, routine execution roles are reducing.Repetitive reporting, manual testing, basic operational support and rule-based processing face pressure as AI and automation reshape work. The report does not suggest that all these jobs will disappear; rather, salary growth may slow unless workers move towards higher-value responsibilities.“Those in repetitive reporting, manual testing, and basic support are most exposed. The route up is adjacency, not reinvention: a BI analyst into data engineering, a sysadmin into cloud, a QA or IAM specialist into security and governance. Pair one technical skill with deep sector knowledge, and keep proof of work that moves a business outcome,” Neeti Sharma says.Not only that, this shift also has implications for how professionals approach career development.So if you are planning to upskill to keep yourself relevant, understand that it should not be driven solely by the popularity of a technology or the prospect of a higher salary.“Instead, employees should identify the capabilities emerging as critical within their industry, understand how these capabilities address business needs and build demonstrable expertise through practical application,” Milind Shah advises.
Article Summary: India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill- differentiated compensation. Specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.

Article Title: 'India an important ally': US state secy Rubio explains why Trump paused sanctions on Russia oil buyers
Article Text:
Marco Rubio says US President studying impact of possible tariffs

India’s energy needs in focus

Energy supply pressures add to the uncertainty

What the waiver means under the Graham Act

Diesel deal with Russia preceded the waiver

US President Donald Trump has waived key sanctions provisions under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, putting on hold proposed tariffs targeting major buyers of Russian oil and gas, including India and China.Rubio, explaining the decision on Saturday (local time), said that the administration wanted 60 days to assess the implications of imposing the measures. He cited India’s continued reliance on Russian oil, its importance as a US ally and mounting pressure on global energy supplies among the factors being considered.While India has diversified its energy sources, it continues to obtain a substantial amount of energy from Russia, Rubio said, adding that shifting away from these supplies could not happen overnight.The law would have allowed the US to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas, including India and China. The waiver has put the relevant provisions on hold while the administration evaluates their potential impact."These sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries—India, for example, and others.And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio said.Rubio’s remarks put India’s energy requirements and its relationship with Washington at the centre of the explanation for the pause. While India has voluntarily diversified its energy portfolio, it continues to source a substantial amount of energy from Russia. According to Rubio, shifting away from these supplies cannot happen overnight."You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next. But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States. So we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he added.Rubio is scheduled to visit India later this month, including Jamnagar, which is home to one of the world's largest refineries.The administration is also weighing developments in the wider geopolitical landscape since the Graham bill was passed. Rubio pointed to growing pressure on global energy supplies, including the conflict involving Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia, the situation around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, and the Russia-Ukraine war.He said attacks on energy infrastructure linked to the war between Russia and Ukraine were also affecting global prices. The expanding range of pressures on energy supplies, he indicated, made it necessary to study the likely consequences of the proposed measures before deciding how to proceed."I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran and not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit, and so that's having an impact on global prices as well," he said.The pause, therefore, gives the US administration time to consider the consequences of targeting countries that buy Russian energy while global supplies face pressure from multiple conflicts.Trump invoked Section 115 of the Graham Act on Friday. The provision authorises the President to waive the application of sanctions against a foreign person, restrictions relating to a person, and duties under the law."I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act," Trump said in the order.The waiver applies to duties under Sections 112 and 113 of the Act. These provisions allowed Trump to increase duties on all goods imported into the US from Russia to as much as 500% ad valorem, meaning duties calculated relative to the value of the goods.They also allowed duties of up to 100% ad valorem on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas. India and China were among the countries covered by this provision.The decision came after Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Russia. Under the arrangement, Russia would immediately supply more than 3,00,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, followed by another 5,00,000 tonnes during November and 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter.Rubio’s explanation for the waiver centred on the need to assess the economic consequences of the proposed tariffs and sanctions, India’s continued energy dependence on Russia despite diversification, and the pressure on global supplies amid geopolitical conflicts.The 60-day window is intended to give the administration time to examine these factors before determining the appropriate combination of measures.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has waived key sanctions provisions under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. The law would have allowed the US to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas. The waiver has put the relevant provisions on hold while the administration evaluates their potential impact.

Article Title: Venezuela signs 61 oil agreements, expects $76 billion in investments over five years
Article Text:
Venezuela signs 61 oil agreements

Venezuela expects to attract nearly $76 billion in oil investments over the next five years under recently signed agreements, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday. A bilateral accord with the United States includes plans to drill 250 rigs and covers 17 oilfields, forming part of a broader package of 61 agreements signed by the two sides.Rodriguez said the proposed investments would deliver direct gains for Venezuela while also benefiting its partners."Major investments are coming," she said. "We are talking about investment of almost $76 billion over five years. Those investments will translate into direct benefits for our country in a win-win partnership, because our partner will also benefit."The agreements come as Venezuela opens up its energy sector to overseas investors following the removal of President Nicolas Maduro in January. The process has the backing of US President Donald Trump's administration.The proposed investments could help lift oil production in a country that holds the world's largest proven crude oil reserves but is producing far less than it did a decade ago.Rodriguez also cited rising output in Zulia, a western Venezuelan state, where production has climbed from 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 370,000 bpd.She expects output to reach 400,000 bpd by the end of this year, although she did not specify when the increase from 70,000 bpd began.The country's oil sector has struggled with prolonged underinvestment, operational difficulties at state-owned oil company PDVSA and US sanctions targeting the energy industry.Meanwhile, Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, appeared in a US court earlier this week as they prepared to respond to an expanded indictment accusing them of conspiring to torture political opponents.The new charges, brought last Thursday, broaden the criminal case against the former Venezuelan president, 63, and Flores, 70. Both had earlier pleaded not guilty to allegations that they abused their positions to help drug traffickers transport cocaine. Their lawyers have also said they deny the torture allegations.The couple were captured by the US military in a raid ordered by Trump in January and subsequently flown to New York.
Article Summary: Venezuela expects to attract nearly $76 billion in oil investments over the next five years. A bilateral accord with the United States includes plans to drill 250 rigs and cover 17 oilfields. The proposed investments could help lift oil production in a country that holds world's largest proven crude oil reserves.

Article Title: Market recap: Top-10 firms add Rs 3.65 lakh crore in mcap; TCS leads the gains
Article Text:
Top-10 firms add Rs 3.65 lakh crore in mcap

A strong week in the stock market added Rs 3.65 lakh crore to the combined market value of nine of India’s top-10 most valued firms. TCS led the gains, followed by Bharti Airtel and Infosys. Larsen & Toubro was the only firm in the group to see its market value fall.The rally saw BSE Sensex gain 2,256.94 points, or 3.11%, over the week, while NSE Nifty rose 625.7 points, or 2.77%.The recovery in the domestic market was particularly strong in information technology stocks, following encouraging September quarter earnings. Renewed buying in several heavyweight stocks also supported the gains, according to Ponmudi R, CEO of online trading and wealth tech firm Enrich Money."The rally was primarily driven by a sharp rebound in information technology stocks following encouraging September quarter earnings, supported by renewed buying interest in several heavyweight stocks," Ponmudi R, CEO - Enrich Money told PTI.TCS emerged as the biggest gainer among the top-10 firms, adding Rs 1,08,542.63 crore to its market capitalisation, which reached Rs 8,91,134.96 crore during the week.Bharti Airtel's valuation increased by Rs 61,406.53 crore to Rs 11,88,815.45 crore, while Infosys gained Rs 55,893.05 crore to reach Rs 4,71,409.41 crore.Reliance Industries added Rs 53,047.56 crore to its market value, taking it to Rs 16,37,437.19 crore and retaining its position as the country's most valued domestic firm.Among the banks, HDFC Bank's market capitalisation climbed by Rs 32,379.05 crore to Rs 11,22,628.07 crore. ICICI Bank recorded a rise of Rs 30,769.95 crore, bringing its valuation to Rs 10,02,871.44 crore.Bajaj Finance also saw a substantial increase, with its market value rising by Rs 14,786.65 crore to Rs 6,11,326.72 crore. LIC added Rs 4,933.5 crore to reach Rs 5,02,204.82 crore, while State Bank of India's valuation increased by Rs 3,323.07 crore to Rs 8,87,722.84 crore.Larsen & Toubro was the sole company among the top-10 to register a decline. Its market capitalisation dropped by Rs 9,232.26 crore to Rs 4,99,725.06 crore.At the end of the week, the ranking of India's most valued domestic companies remained led by Reliance Industries, followed by Bharti Airtel, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, TCS, State Bank of India, Bajaj Finance, LIC, Larsen & Toubro and Infosys.
Article Summary: TCS led the gains, followed by Bharti Airtel and Infosys. Larsen & Toubro was the only firm in the group to see its market value fall. BSE Sensex gained 2,256.94 points, or 3.11%, over the week.

Article Title: Refined in India, bound for West: Russian-crude fuel exports to Europe rise 43%
Article Text:
Indian refiners' fuel exports to the West jump 43% as they keep processing Russian crude

Jamnagar refinery leads exports to the West

EU ban on Russian crude products has a loophole

India's Russian crude imports fall 13% in September

India spends 4.1 billion euros on Russian fossil fuels

Why India turned to Russian oil

Russian crude is finding its way to Western markets through Indian refineries, with countries including the EU, Australia, the US and New Zealand buying oil products worth 1 billion euros ($1.2 billion) in September.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei shipped these products to sanctioned countries, with export values rising 43% since August, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).The EU was the biggest buyer of oil products from the three countries, importing shipments worth 667 million euros. Australia followed with 168 million euros, while the US bought products worth 154 million euros and New Zealand imported 19 million euros’ worth.CREA estimated that 295 million euros’ worth of the products exported had been refined from Russian crude.India’s Reliance Industries-operated Jamnagar refinery in Gujarat supplied six of the seven cargoes unloaded at European Union ports in September, despite the bloc’s ban on oil products refined from Russian crude, which took effect in January 2026.Jamnagar also accounted for the largest share of the group’s exports to the US, with shipments worth 122 million euros.Russian crude made up 32% of the refinery’s crude imports between July and September.Of the seven shipments unloaded at EU ports in September, Italy received three, Romania two, and Spain and Cyprus one each.The value of exports reported as destined for EU ports from refineries processing Russian crude rose 80% during the month. These included a 104,000-tonne cargo of gasoil, or diesel, from Jamnagar that was still on its way to Rotterdam.The EU banned imports of oil products refined from Russian crude in January 2026. However, the restrictions exempt net crude exporters. CREA said this leaves a loophole because a country can export more crude than it imports while still processing Russian-origin oil at its refineries.The research group has recommended applying the ban at the refinery level. Under its proposal, oil products from any refinery that has processed Russian crude in the previous six months would be prohibited, regardless of the declared origin of the finished product.This is a recommendation by CREA, an advocacy group, and not existing policy.While exports of refined products to sanctioning countries rose, India’s imports of Russian crude fell 13% in September. This was the second consecutive monthly decline and the lowest level since April, CREA said.Imports dropped at all three of India’s largest importing refineries. Intake at Jamnagar fell 27% from August, while Indian Oil Corporation’s (IOC) Paradip refinery recorded a 21% decline. Nayara Energy’s Vadinar refinery saw imports fall 8%."Despite the decline, Vadinar overtook Jamnagar as India's largest importer of Russian crude."Smaller facilities also recorded lower imports. The HMEL Mundra Oil Terminal reduced its intake by 74%, while the Kochi refinery saw a 32% month-on-month decline.IOC’s Mundra Oil Terminal was the exception, receiving 570,000 tonnes of Russian crude in September after importing none in August."The main exception was the IOC Mundra Oil Terminal, which received 570 thousand tonnes of Russian crude in September after receiving none in August," CREA said.Despite the monthly decline in crude purchases, India remained Russia’s second-largest buyer of fossil fuels in September, spending 4.1 billion euros on Russian hydrocarbons. China was the only country that bought more."India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in September 2026, importing a total of 4.1 billion euros of Russian hydrocarbons. Crude oil constituted 88 per cent of India's purchases, totalling 3.6 billion euros. Coal (309 million euros) and oil products (161 million euros) constituted the remainder of its monthly Russian imports," CREA said.Since December 2022, India has accounted for 37% of Russia’s crude exports, compared with China’s 50%.India was a marginal buyer of Russian oil before Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Its purchases increased after Western buyers pulled back and Russia began selling crude at steep discounts.Urals crude averaged $90.7 a barrel in September but continued to trade $23 below Brent crude. The discount remained unchanged from August.The decline in India’s Russian crude imports was not driven by US pressure alone, according to analysts at Kpler. Tighter supplies and stronger competition from China for Russian oil also contributed to the fall in volumes.Kpler expects India’s Russian crude imports to remain between 1.8 million and 1.9 million barrels per day in October.
Article Summary: Indian refiners' fuel exports to the West jump 43% as they keep processing Russian crude. EU banned imports of oil products refined from Russian crude in January 2026. However, the restrictions exempt net crude exporters. India's imports of Russian crude fell 13% in September.

Article Title: Private banks’ profits rise, large lenders see margin pressure
Article Text:
Some mid-sized private lenders and public sector banks recorded an expansion in NIM

MUMBAI: Private sector banks reported higher profits in the Sept-quarter despite the top three banks seeing pressure on net interest margins (NIM).The FCNR(B) deposits boosted the deposit growth rate to a decadal high and expanded balance sheets, but cost of deposits rose because of the higher rate being offered under the special scheme to NRIs.The three largest private sector lenders by assets — HDFC Bank ICICI Bank and Axis Bank — reported margin compression in the second quarter as funding costs rose and deposit competition intensified. Axis Bank saw the sharpest decline, with NIM falling 37 basis points year on year (YoY) to 3.36% from 3.73%. Its net profit rose 37.6% to Rs 7,003 crore, supported by non-interest income and controlled credit costs.ICICI Bank’s NIM fell 12 basis points to 4.18% from 4.3%, while net profit rose 20.1% to Rs 14,843 crore, aided by growth in advances. HDFC Bank’s margin decl­ined 11 basis points to 3.16% from 3.27%, while net profit grew 4.7% to Rs 19,510 crore as it continued to adjust its credit-to-deposit ratio after merger with HDFC Ltd.YES Bank reported a 65% YoY increase in net profit to Rs 1,080 crore for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, driven by higher net interest income and lower provisions. However, the bank said that if the Supreme Court order quashing the write-down of Rs 8,415 crore of AT-1 bonds had been factored in, it would have reported a loss of Rs 5,217 crore and net worth of Rs 46,970 crore, ag­a­inst the reported Rs 53,268 crore.Its NIM rose 10 basis points to 2.6% from 2.5%.HDFC Bank’s margins also reflected the cost of raising $7 billion through FCNR(B) deposits at a we­i­g­h­ted average landed cost of 6% to 6.25%, along with a hi­g­her share of non-retail assets and liabilities. The ba­nk expects margins to rec­o­ver over the coming quarters as lending rates reprice faster than funding costs, although rebalancing the asset mix will take two to three quarters. Its CASA ratio has weakened as households shift savings to higher-yie­lding instruments and the bank replaces matu­ring wh­o­lesale borrowings with bu­lk deposits. It has also chosen to concede mortgage market share rather than offer home loans at ra­tes that would dilute profitability.Some mid-sized private lenders and public sector banks recorded an expansion in NIM. Federal Bank’s margin rose 26 basis points to 3.32% from 3.06%, while net profit increased 45% to Rs 1,386 crore. Central Bank of India’s NIM expanded 12 basis points to 3.01% from 2.89%, supporting a 21% increase in net profit to Rs 1,469 crore. IDBI Bank recorded the largest margin expansion among the lenders in the comparison, with NIM rising 40 basis points to 4.11% from 3.71%. Its net profit, however, fell 39% to Rs 2,206 crore, reflecting higher provisions or a normalisation of non-core income against a high base.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank ICICI Bank and Axis Bank reported margin compression in the second quarter. Axis Bank saw the sharpest decline, with NIM falling 37 basis points year on year. Some mid-sized private lenders and public sector banks recorded an expansion in NIM.

Article Title: AI is changing Asia’s jobs market: What it means for India
Article Text:
AI is changing Asia’s jobs market

Businesses using AI see stronger labour demand

Lower AI exposure may not be an advantage for India in the long run

Skills and preparedness will shape the employment outlook

Asia has a tricky tightrope to walk as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes its job market: creating enough jobs for a growing workforce while ensuring workers don’t get left behind as technology changes the rules of the game.The challenge is particularly significant for India, Indonesia and the Philippines, where expanding working-age populations need productive employment even as AI transforms industries expected to provide those jobs.The International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific points to a shift in employer demand since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. An analysis of approximately 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies found that demand for jobs more exposed to AI had declined by nearly 10 per cent compared with occupations less exposed to the technology.However, the trend does not suggest that AI is simply eliminating jobs. The report found that the decline in demand for workers in highly exposed occupations appears to have stabilised, despite significant advances in AI capabilities.Part of the changing employment landscape is being driven by demand for new technical skills. Prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation and AI agent development are among the areas creating new employment opportunities.Employers are looking for people who can put AI to practical use in business operations, integrate it into existing processes and improve productivity.How companies use the technology is emerging as an important factor in determining its employment impact. Around 6 per cent of firms in Asia explicitly seek AI skills in their job advertisements, according to the IMF report, highlighting the uneven pace of adoption across businesses.Firms that have adopted AI are seeing stronger growth in labour demand than those that have not. This pattern also holds for occupations highly exposed to automation, indicating that the technology can support human capabilities even as it reduces the demand for certain tasks.The employment effects of AI, therefore, vary according to how businesses incorporate it into their operations. Alongside the decline in demand for some AI-exposed occupations, the report identifies stronger labour demand growth among firms adopting the technology.Emerging Asian economies, including India, may initially face less disruption because many workers are employed in agriculture and other sectors less exposed to AI. But this could create a longer-term difficulty if the technology makes it harder for workers to move into higher-productivity manufacturing and services.For countries with growing working-age populations, the challenge extends beyond protecting existing jobs. They must also create productive employment opportunities and enable workers to move into occupations that can support higher productivity.India, Indonesia and the Philippines will need to navigate these pressures as AI reshapes the sectors expected to employ their expanding workforces. The pace and effectiveness of adaptation by businesses, workers and economies will be crucial to how this transition unfolds.The IMF report places the emphasis on preparing workers and institutions for the changes ahead, rather than focusing solely on the adoption of AI. Education reform, reskilling, digital infrastructure and stronger labour-market institutions will be central to this effort.Businesses will need to invest in workers as they integrate AI into their operations. Governments, meanwhile, will have to prepare younger populations for changing skill requirements and evolving occupational opportunities.Asia’s ability to manage the transition will depend on how well it combines technological progress with workforce preparedness. Timely investment in skills could help the region use AI-driven changes to support productivity, innovation and sustainable employment, while keeping inclusive growth within reach.
Article Summary: The International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific points to a shift in employer demand since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. Demand for jobs more exposed to AI had declined by nearly 10 per cent compared with occupations less exposed to the technology. But the trend does not suggest that AI is simply eliminating jobs.

Article Title: India on track for historic growth streakas global bodies raise forecasts above 7%
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Going by projections by global agencies, India is on course to surpass its 2003-2007 record of five consecutive years of 7% or higher growth, Kyunghoon Kim of Korea Institute for International Economic Policy said.Starting 2021, India has recorded a five-year average annual growth rate of 7.83%, marking the second-highest five-year average since 1960, Kim said in a social media post. Between 2003 and 2007, the economy had expanded at an average pace of 7.89%. “Sustaining such momentum over several years deserves attention,” Kim said.Following a 5.8% contraction during the pandemic, India’s economy rebounded sharply by 9.7% in 2021 and has sustained growth exceeding 7% in each subsequent year.After a 7.8% growth in the June quarter, most global outfits — from IMF and World Bank to OECD and rating agencies — have revised their projections to around 7% growth this year, making India the fastest growth major economy once again.Kim highlighted that the latest round of growth is on an expanded base as India’s GDP stood at over $1 trillion in 2007 and is now approaching $4 trillion. A 7% expansion now delivers larger absolute additions to national output.“It is projected to become the world’s third-largest economy around 2030,” he said.While structural and global headwinds remain, he noted that maintaining such sustained high-velocity growth across a population of 1.4 billion represents a milestone achievement. “I hope economists at major institutions and I will once again be adding a few decimal points to our forecasts when the next quarterly GDP figures arrive,” he said.
Article Summary: India is on course to surpass its 2003-2007 record of five consecutive years of 7% or higher growth. Between 2003 and 2007, the economy had expanded at an average pace of 7.89%. “Sustaining such momentum over several years deserves attention,” Kyunghoon Kim said.

Article Title: Tata Trusts to build institutions, not just fund them: Noel
Article Text:
Noel cast the shift as a return to the founders’ purpose

MUMBAI: Tata Trusts will put more weight on building institutions directly rather than only funding them, chairman Noel Tata said, as the charitable body’s differences with the Tata Sons board persist.In the Trusts’ FY26 annual report, Noel said the need was “not simply to support an existing effort, but to build institutions and models that can become enduring public assets in their own right”. He did not directly refer to the governance and strategic differences between the Trusts and Tata Sons.The Trusts, which draw dividends from Tata Sons, disbursed Rs 1,556 crore in FY26. Institutional grants took Rs 1,353 crore. Individuals received Rs 203 crore. The Trusts have long worked mainly through grants and funding support.Noel cast the shift as a return to the founders’ purpose. “Our founders did not set out to build the largest group of companies,” he wrote. “They believed that enterprise carried with it a responsibility to society, and that the true measure of progress was an improvement in the quality of people’s lives.”Its earlier institutions include Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru and Mumbai’s Tata Hospital.Noel named education as a priority. India needed more institutions that nurture talent at home, he said, so students are not forced to look overseas. In healthcare, the Trusts are working towards a network of 40-50 not-for-profit general hospitals.
Article Summary: Noel cast the shift as a return to the founders’ purpose. He did not directly refer to the governance and strategic differences between the Trusts and Tata Sons. The Trusts, which draw dividends from Tata Sons, disbursed Rs 1,556 crore in FY26.

Article Title: Ahead of Reliance Industries investing in Texas refinery, Rubio to meet Ambani in Jamnagar
Article Text:
The trip to Gujarat’s refinery hub, where he will visit the Reliance oil refining complex, is expected to last around nine hours

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai Tuesday for a two-day visit to India that will see him travelling to Jamnagar as well. While his bilateral with counterpart S Jaishankar is scheduled for Tuesday in Mumbai, he will travel to Jamnagar the next day.The trip to Gujarat’s refinery hub, where he will visit the Reliance oil refining complex, is expected to last around nine hours. Rubio will also have a meeting with Mukesh Ambani before returning to Mumbai.The visit highlights growing India-US energy cooperation. Rubio is expected to focus on strategic energy partnerships, highlighting the importance of the Reliance oil refinery as the company prepares for its upcoming investment in a Texas oil refinery. Officials did not confirm or deny reports that Rubio may also visit the Vantara animal rehabilitation centre, located in the same complex.On his arrival in Mumbai, Rubio will briefly meet Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis and lay a wreath at the Taj Hotel memorial before joining Jaishankar for the bilateral meeting.This will be Rubio’s second bilateral meeting with Jaishankar in India this year, following his visit in May.They will meet again later this month on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta. Jaishankar is expected to prioritise India’s concerns related to immigration-related issues, while reviewing bilateral cooperation, reaffirming commitment to the trade deal under discussion and reiterating India’s position on energy security.Later in the evening, Jaishankar will join Rubio for the Freedom 250 reception to celebrate the US’s 250th anniversary at Jio Convention Centre. The ministry of external affairs has said Jaishankar will be the guest of honour. Although an official confirmation is still awaited, Rubio is also likely to meet Gautam Adani and Tata group chief N Chandrasekaran before his departure for Jamnagar Wednesday.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai Tuesday for a two-day visit to India. While his bilateral with counterpart S Jaishankar is scheduled for Tuesday in Mumbai, he will travel to Jamnagar the next day. The trip to Gujarat’s refinery hub, where he will visit the Reliance oil refining complex, is expected to last around nine hours.

Article Title: Dubai-based woman invests 3.41 crore in FCNR deposits along with husband, gets tax notice for unexplained money; ITAT gives relief saying bank confirmed source and AO mistook yen for rupees
Article Text:
ITAT Jaipur identified a significant error in the AO's assessment. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the woman win the case in ITAT?

Indians based globally and investing in India can in some cases face tax notices for unexplained income.In one such case, a woman invested money in FCNR term deposits along with her husband. Both of them received separate tax notices from the Income Tax Department for unexplained income worth crores.A woman, who originally hails from Beawar, and now resides in Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE), decided to put money into investments in India. She along with her husband invested Rs 3.41 crore in two Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) term deposits.The husband’s name appeared as the first holder of both deposits, with the woman listed as the second holder. The funds were accordingly transferred from Dubai to his Non-Resident External (NRE) account in a bank in India.Also Read | Man skipped filing ITR and got tax notice so he declared Rs 12.9 lakh income; department imposed 200% penalty of Rs 3.99 lakh on taxable amount, but ITAT cancels it The husband chose to hold the deposits in Japanese yen (JPY). The first deposit, worth 1.726 crore JPY, was opened on October 14, 2017, followed by a second deposit of 1.658 crore JPY on February 21, 2018, according to an ET report.Despite jointly holding the FCNR deposits, the husband and his wife received separate income tax notices alleging unexplained money under Section 69A of the Income-tax Act.This article focuses on the woman’s legal battle against the notice seeking to treat the deposits as unexplained money in her hands under Section 69A.On September 22, 2026, the woman secured relief from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Jaipur.ITAT Jaipur noted that the Income Tax Department had issued a notice under Section 133(6) to the concerned bank on November 9, 2022, seeking information about the transactions. In its response, the bank confirmed the transactions and provided details of the source of the funds.The tribunal observed that the relevant information was therefore already available with the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO). It also noted that the department had neither challenged the authenticity of the bank statements nor disputed the correctness of the assessment made in the woman’s husband's case.Also Read | Man worked in South Korea and received salary in US dollars in NRE account, income tax department sent notice; ITAT Bangalore sets aside assessment and orders fresh review ITAT Jaipur identified a significant error in the AO's assessment. The officer had mistakenly interpreted the amounts recorded in Japanese yen (JPY) as figures in Indian rupees.Pointing out the discrepancy, the tribunal said the combined principal of the two deposits was JPY 3.384 crore, comprising JPY 1.726 crore and JPY 1.658 crore. However, the equivalent amount invested in Indian currency was Rs 2 crore. The addition of Rs 3.41 crore made by the AO did not correspond to any amount in rupees found in the woman’s possession.The tribunal examined the bank statements and found that both FCNR deposits had been funded through debits from a jointly held NRE savings account. Before each debit, the account had received a credit of Rs 1 crore through the banking channel. The transaction narration carried the name of the woman’s husband and the first holder of the deposits.The ITAT Jaipur said: “The immediate source is thus identified from the bank’s own record and points to the first holder. The Income Tax Department has not alleged, much less shown, that these funds arose from any source in India.”The tribunal explained that Section 69A applies when a person is found to own money but fails to provide an explanation, or offers an explanation that is not satisfactory, regarding its nature and source.Also Read | Man had Rs 2 crore bank deposit and didn’t file ITR, faced Rs 2.51 crore tax addition; ITAT Chennai quashes reassessment after Income Tax Department missed 6-year deadline by 5 days In this case, however, the woman was the second holder of the FCNR deposits, while her husband was the first holder. Since the source of the money in the deposits had been explained by her husband, the tribunal found that the same funds could not be treated as unexplained money in the hands of the woman merely because she was the second holder.ITAT Jaipur also considered the discrepancy in the records concerning the woman’s residential status. The CIT(A) had recorded her status as a non-resident, which was consistent with her Dubai address and the NRE and FCNR accounts reflected in the bank statements.However, the AO's assessment order classified her as a resident without recording any finding to support that conclusion. The tribunal therefore treated the woman as a non-resident.Under Section 5(2) of the Income-tax Act, income earned by a non-resident is taxable in India only if it is received or deemed to be received in India, or accrues or arises, or is deemed to accrue or arise, in the country. ITAT Jaipur observed that the department had not identified any income meeting these conditions in the woman’s case.Rahul Jain, Partner at Khaitan & Co, explained to ET that the Indian tax liability of a non-resident Indian (NRI) generally extends only to income earned in India or received in the country. However, interest earned by a non-resident on funds held in an NRE account with an Indian bank is specifically exempt from Indian income tax. The principal amount deposited in an NRE account is also generally not taxable in India.In this case, the tax authorities treated the entire amount held in the NRE account, covering both the principal and interest, as unexplained money and sought to tax it under Section 69A of the Income-tax Act, 1961.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing parties Section 69A deals with money, bullion, jewellery or other valuable articles owned by a taxpayer for which the person either fails to explain the nature and source of acquisition or provides an explanation that the tax authorities do not find satisfactory.During the appeal, the woman explained that her husband was the first holder of the disputed FCNR deposits and that the money had come from another jointly held NRE account with the same bank. She also submitted the relevant bank statements to support her explanation.Another significant factor was that the same jurisdictional tax officer had examined her husband's explanation concerning the very same deposits and accepted it. Taking these circumstances into account, the CIT(A) ruled in the woman’s favour and deleted the additions made by the tax officer.The matter subsequently came before the ITAT Jaipur, which observed that the tax authorities had not challenged the authenticity of the bank statements submitted by the woman.ITAT Jaipur consequently upheld the CIT(A)'s order in her favour, confirming the deletion of the tax addition relating to the alleged unexplained money.
Article Summary: A woman, who originally hails from Beawar, and now resides in Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE), decided to put money into investments in India. She along with her husband invested Rs 3.41 crore in two Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) term deposits. Both of them received separate tax notices from the Income Tax Department for unexplained income worth crores.

Article Title: Jamnagar on Rubio's two-day itinerary: Musk mellows on Reliance, ‘appreciates’ post
Article Text:
US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in India and will visit the world’s largest oil refinery in Jamnagar

NEW DELHI: Elon Musk 's blow-hot-and-cold stand for getting Starlink access to India has now entered a conciliatory phase after the tech trillionaire was all fire on X last week. The change in tone comes at a time when US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in India and will visit the world's largest oil refinery in Jamnagar that's owned by Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani - who was targeted by Musk last week."Much appreciated," Musk said on X late Friday night in response to Reliance Industries' first reply to his charges on Friday, in which Mukesh Ambani's conglomerate had said: "We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must... abide by the laws and policies of the land.... As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances."Starlink also responded to Reliance's post, saying it has "worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for five plus years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet."Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani's Reliance Jio and Musk's Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service so that remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. Starlink clearance is being seen as part of the larger Indo-US ties with several factors being part of the play, including the trade deal and threat of tariffs over buying Russian oil.
Article Summary: Elon Musk's blow-hot-and-cold stand for getting Starlink access to India has now entered a conciliatory phase. The change in tone comes at a time when US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in India and will visit the world’s largest oil refinery in Jamnagar.

Article Title: Covid blues over? Hotel tariffs in Delhi, Mumbai overtake Rishikesh, Ranthambore for 1st time post pandemic
Article Text:
(Representative image)

NEW DELHI: For the first time since Covid, the leisure and spiritual destinations — Ranthambore and Rishikesh — have been overtaken by Mumbai and Delhi as the Indian cities with highest average hotel tariffs. Leading hospitality consulting firm Hotelivate’s recently released trends & opportunities report for 2026 shows average revenue per available room (RevPAR) for Delhi at Rs 9,811; Mumbai Rs 9,761; Ranthambore Rs 9,649 and Rishikesh Rs 9,583 in FY 2025-26. In the previous fiscal, the top four positions were Ranthambore (Rs 0,059), Rishikesh (Rs 9,493), Mumbai (Rs 9,458) and Delhi (Rs 8,846). This shows a revival in corporate travel, international visitation and the group-oriented Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (MICE) activity.Varanasi has shown a big jump in average tariffs with the holy city boasting of the fifth highest rates at Rs 8,857 — ahead of Udaipur (Rs 8,414) and Goa (Rs 7,614) — in FY 26, up from the ninth spot in previous fiscal when its RevPAR was Rs 6,769.The deadly Pahalgam terror attack last April saw Srinagar register its biggest fall in visitors. “Srinagar recorded the sharpest decline across the dataset, with RevPAR falling 51.9% year-on-year (to Rs 3,323 in FY 26) and the market moving from among the country’s leading performers to the bottom 15.Jalandhar, Jammu and Amritsar faced similar pressures, as cancellations associated with Operation Sindoor weakened demand across markets closer to the border,” says the report.“In recent years, leisure destinations, particularly emerging markets with limited supply and demand from destination weddings, (had) risen sharply in the national rankings. In 2025/26, however, Delhi and Mumbai emerged as the country’s leading RevPAR markets.… Leisure destinations such as Ranthambore, Rishikesh and Udaipur nevertheless remained among the top performers,” says the report.“The gap at the top also narrowed considerably, with less than Rs 250 separating the four leading markets, compared with a much wider spread in the previous year. Strong performance in these leisure destinations has attracted additional midmarket and upper midmarket supply, resulting in some normalisation in market-wide rates without displacing them from the country’s leading RevPAR markets,” it added.At the end of March 2026, India had a pipeline of 1.6 lakh hotel rooms to open in next five years. This was a 41% jump from the pipeline of 1.1 lakh exactly a year ago. “The pipeline is now approaching the scale of the country’s existing branded inventory. If it materialises in full, India’s branded hotel inventory would increase by 77% to approximately 3.7 lakh rooms. The top five markets are likely to be relatively unchanged with one exception; Jaipur is likely to surpass Chennai to become the fifth largest market in the country by operating inventory. However, not all of this supply is expected to materialise,” it said.
Article Summary: For the first time since Covid, the leisure and spiritual destinations — Ranthambore and Rishikesh — have been overtaken by Mumbai and Delhi as the Indian cities with highest average hotel tariffs. Varanasi has shown a big jump in average tariffs with the holy city boasting of the fifth highest rates at Rs 8,857.

Article Title: The Indian growth story: Why the post-pandemic boom is different
Article Text:
As per latest IMF projections, India is expected to become the third largest economy after the US and China by 2031.

The post pandemic era

Five consecutive years of growth above 7%

GDP Growth Forecasts See Sharp Upward Revisions

India's GDP Growth Forecasts See Upward Revisions

India may have slipped to the sixth spot in the list of the world’s largest economies, but its GDP growth continues to defy estimates by both domestic and global institutions. At 7% plus, India is the world’s fastest growing major economy and what stands out in the current phase is the resilience amid multiple, persistent, and emerging global uncertainties.Kyunghoon Kim, Head of India & South Asia Team at Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP) has said that India’s growth has set to surpass 7% for the fifth consecutive year.“India’s economy rebounded by 9.7% in 2021, then grew by more than 7% in each of the next four years. That makes five consecutive years of growth above 7%, matching the 2003–2007 run, when India attracted global attention as one of the BRIC economies,” he says in a thread on X (formerly Twitter).In the post, Kim noted that India’s average annual economic growth between 2021 and 2025 was 7.83%. This was the second-highest five-year average in data going back to 1960, just behind the 7.89% recorded between 2003 and 2007.India’s economy contracted by 5.8% in 2020 during the pandemic before rebounding with growth of 9.7% in 2021. It then expanded by more than 7% in each of the following four years, according to Kim.Kim said that if current forecasts hold, India could surpass that record.He also pointed to how economists, including himself, have repeatedly revised their growth projections upwards as quarterly GDP figures came in stronger than expected.The point of his comparison was not simply the sharp rebound after the pandemic, but the economy’s ability to sustain rapid growth over several subsequent years.Several things stand out in this growth: for one, the economy is now operating on a completely different scale.As Kim notes, India’s GDP was just over $1 trillion in 2007; now it is nearly $4 trillion. “The same 7% growth rate therefore represents a much larger expansion,” he says.In 2020, when the Covid pandemic dealt a major blow to the global economy, India too took a major hit to its economy and GDP contracted sharply. Since then, the economy’s bounceback has been stronger than expected, consistently beating estimates by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).At the end of FY2021, the size of the Indian economy by nominal GDP was $2.6 trillion. At the end of FY2027, it is projected to be $4.15 trillion - that’s an almost 60% rise in just six years despite the pandemic, Russia-Ukraine war, Trump’s trade policies and 50% tariffs, and now the ongoing US-Iran war.What’s also noteworthy is that India depends on the world for 90% of its crude oil needs and the US-Iran conflict choked a crucial oil supply passage for the country - the Strait of Hormuz. Economists around the world warned that the Indian economy would see a notable hit from the war. Yet, the first quarter estimates of 7.8% have beaten all estimates. Inflation has risen, but it is still within RBI’s target range.So what’s working for India?It’s the size of its domestic market and a demographic dividend that is paying off along with key reforms by the government and a proactive monetary policy management by the RBI. The country has been pushing for self-sufficiency and schemes like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme have made it into a key export hub, especially for electronics.Kim acknowledged that India continues to face challenges, while arguing that its economic performance deserves attention given the country’s population of around 1.4 billion.Kim also highlighted recent upward revisions to India’s growth outlook by major institutions. According to him the upgrades are particularly notable when viewed against India’s growth record since the pandemic.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised its growth projection for India in the current year from 6.4% to 7%. The revision follows similar upgrades by several other institutions, including the World Bank, Asian Development Bank (ADB), S&P and Moody's.These changes came after official figures put India's GDP growth in the first quarter at 7.8%. Most international agencies now expect the economy to expand by 6.9% to 7% in the current fiscal year.IMF has endorsed India's revised approach to calculating gross domestic product, saying the new methodology conforms to sound statistical practices and recommendations made by the international financial institution.Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, called the change a "welcome development". He said India's updated method of measuring GDP was consistent with the guidance issued by the IMF's statistics department.In its latest World Economic Outlook, the IMF said that the global economy has remained resilient despite several shocks in recent years, projecting worldwide growth of 3.4% in 2026.India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7%. This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity," the IMF said.India and Germany have recorded the largest upward revisions to their growth forecasts. In contrast, Saudi Arabia's economy is projected to contract by 3.3% this year, following a five-percentage-point reduction in its growth outlook.Explaining India's improved prospects, the IMF said: "India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms.”The report also drew attention to India's efforts to broaden its trade relationships. It cited the country's trade agreements with the UK and the European Union, which are expected to reduce tariffs and ease restrictions on services trade. These arrangements could also "facilitate adjustments to recent trade policy changes".US tariff measures have prompted countries around the world to pursue a series of trade agreements. India, too, has advanced free trade agreements (FTAs) that had remained under negotiation for years.The Indian economy continues to surprise on the upside, and despite the sharp rupee depreciation which led to its nominal GDP not rising as much in dollar terms, the economy continues to hold strong. As per latest IMF projections, India is expected to become the third largest economy after the US and China by 2031.
Article Summary: India's economy contracted by 5.8% in 2020 during the pandemic before rebounding with growth of 9.7% in 2021. Since then, the economy’s bounceback has been stronger than expected, consistently beating estimates by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) At the end of FY2021, the size of the Indian economy by nominal GDP was $2.6 trillion; by FY2027, it is projected to be $4.15 trillion.
